newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies lower.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs seen steady to lower, pork bellies lower.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.200 cent a bushel lower while pork belly futures were called 0.500 to 1.000 cent lower, livestock analysts said.

Steady to lower indications on cash hogs early Monday linked to reports of reduced packer demand for slaughter hogs were expected to weigh on hog futures. Although pork cutout values rose Friday, packer margins are poor and some are cutting back on the rate of slaughter, analysts said.
Domestic demand for pork is down at current high prices which could offset expectations of increased pork exports due to Taiwan's pork export ban in the hog pit, sources said.

Pork belly futures were expected to be pressured by Friday's bearishly-construed U.S. Cold Storage report. The report showed frozen belly stocks at 54.8 million lbs, above the high end of expectations of 53.2 million lbs, which should stimulate early pressure, analyst said. Futures had risen sharply on Friday in anticipation of a bullish number, they said.
However, underlying support is still anticipated in view of increased export demand for bellies and slow movement of product into storage so far during April, they said.
